entry.title: STL TONEHUB - Raise The Amp Sim Bar

media:group.media:title: STL TONEHUB - Raise The Amp Sim Bar
media:group.media:description:
In this video James from The Studio Rats takes you on a tour of the latest version of ToneHub from STL Tones and shows you just how great this new contender in the guitar capture software battle really is.
This is not just a brief overview, this is a full deep dive tutorial on how to get the best result when capturing your precious amp tone either using the new cloud based processing solution or importing existing NAM captures.
What STL Tones say:
Capture your own rig for ToneHub entirely in the cloud, with improved capture accuracy. Play the Tracer Tone through your gear, upload an existing DI and reamped track, or record straight into the page.
Training runs in the cloud, so there is nothing to install and nothing left running on your computer. Every capture is matched and scored against your own recording, then publishes to ToneHub in a click.
You can find out more about ToneHub and the full STL Tones range at the link below - https://www.stltones.com/collections/plugins

entry.title: The BEST Guitar Pedal Under $100?! - Walrus Audio Fundamental Lo-Fi Delay

media:group.media:title: The BEST Guitar Pedal Under $100?! - Walrus Audio Fundamental Lo-Fi Delay
media:group.media:description:
In today's video, Paul Drew from The Studio Rats is checking out the brand new delay pedal from Walrus Audio from the Fundamental range called LO-FI Delay. I think this could be the best $100 you can spend on any guitar pedal.
To check out the Walrus Audio Fundamental LO-FI Delay Click below.
UK https://andertonsmusiccompany.pxf.io/jR4n1e
Europe https://thmn.to/thoprod/653360?offid=1&affid=3117
USA https://sweetwater.sjv.io/gR7Aor
AM: A bright delay with a high-pass filter, light harmonic distortion, and dual wow and flutter modulation on the repeats that melt away into a hazy backdrop full of character and gentle pitch movement. You’ll hear echoes degrade and thin almost like they’re coming through a fading AM radio signal, creating a texture that works well for dreamy leads, open chords, and washy backdrops. Murk: Dark, dense, and responsive. Murk rolls off the high end and adds heavy distortion with dual low-frequency modulation to push repeats into a thick, undulating cloud. Discover slow modulation that makes the delay compress and expand with the dynamics of your playing, making it ideal for shadowy ambience, brooding melodies, and worn lo-fi textures. Keep Feedback low to add shadowy movement under your riffs. Push it higher to build repeats into a pulsing cloud that swells and shifts around every note. Echo: A rhythmic, multi-tap delay with analog-style tone shaping. At short delay times, the taps gather into dense, lo-fi ambience that sits between an echo and a reverb. At longer delay times, they spread into syncopated, hypnotic patterns that can add movement and cascading trails that weave around your playing, or help you lock into a new groove.

entry.title: PRS FINALLY Made a Guitar I Actually Want to Play!

media:group.media:title: PRS FINALLY Made a Guitar I Actually Want to Play!
media:group.media:description:
In today's video Paul Drew from The Studio Rats is checking out the 2025 PRS Standard 24 Satin. This USA made PRS Core guitar is one of thie only PRS guitars that I can actually see myself playing. As the PRS Standard 24 Satin is a one pice mahogany body, Its less ostentatious that a lot of the PRS USA guitars. The onlt issue with this trully fantastic guitar is the price, at £3500 its most definatly not for the faint hearted.
To check out the PRS Standard 24 Satin Europe https://thmn.to/thocf/1fjmhndtwg
To check out the PRS Standard 24 Satin In the US https://sweetwater.sjv.io/Gb4zXL
The PRS Standard harkens back to Paul Reed Smith’s pre-factory all-mahogany guitars. Its all-mahogany construction promotes a warm, full, midrange-forward tone, and its “sinky” satin nitro finish brings a stripped-down look and roadworthy feel to the instrument.
The PRS Standard 24 features many classic PRS specifications, including a 25” scale length, Pattern Thin neck with a 24-fret, 10” radius rosewood fretboard, PRS Patented Tremolo, and PRS Phase III tuners with unplated brass shafts.
Under the hood, the PRS Standard 24 is outfitted with PRS DMO treble and bass pickups with volume and tone controls and a 5-way blade switch. PRS DMO (Dynamic, Musical, Open) pickups have a “wide open” sound with vocal character, meaning they deliver clear, pleasant-sounding tones across a wide range of frequencies (bass to treble) in each pickup. DMO pickups were personally designed by Paul Reed Smith and the PRS New Products Engineering team. From our own hands-on research into coveted vintage pickup models to advancements in signal analyzation and “tuning” technology, these pickups incorporate every detail of pickup knowledge PRS has gained in recent years of R&D.
